column3: NASB follows the critical text (“on your behalf”); “in the flesh” is rendered “personally.”
NASB follows the critical text (“God's mystery, that is, Christ Himself”); it adds “attaining to,” “comes from,” and “true.”
NASB follows the critical text.
NASB follows the critical text without “now”; “speech” is rendered “argument.”
NASB renders “in the flesh” as “in body,” “good order” as “good discipline,” and “firmness” as “stability.”
NASB adds “so.”
NASB follows the critical text without “in it”; it adds “firmly” and “now” and renders “were taught” as “were instructed.”
NASB renders “take heed” as “See to it” and “principles” as “elementary principles.”
NASB renders “bodily” as “in bodily form.”
NASB renders “completed” as “made complete.”
NASB follows the critical text without “of the sins”; it renders “in the circumcision” as “by the circumcision.”
NASB follows the critical text; “the faith of the working” is rendered “faith in the working.”
NASB follows the critical text (“you”); it adds “when” and “our.”
NASB renders “handwriting” as “certificate of debt.”
NASB renders “in it” as “through Him”; the meaning is uncertain.
NASB follows the critical text (“or”); “judge” is rendered “act as your judge,” and “Sabbaths” is “a Sabbath day.”
NASB adds “mere” and renders “body” as “substance.”

NASB follows the critical text without “not”; it renders “disqualify” as “keep defrauding you of your prize,” “humility” as “self-abasement,” and “detailing” as “taking his stand on visions,” though the meaning is uncertain.
NASB renders “the increase of God” as “a growth which is from God.”
NASB follows the critical text without “therefore”; it adds “such as” and renders “principles” as “elementary principles.”
NASB puts the prohibitions in quotation marks.
NASB puts the first half in parentheses and makes the verse end the question begun in v. 20.
NASB renders “self-imposed worship” as “self-made religion” and “not of any honor” as “of no value.”
